title: Integral finite powers of a geometric semiabelian group
statement: Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Let $G/F$ be a smooth separated commutative group scheme of finite type [def-pc-scheme, def-sc-group-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Separated means that its diagonal is a closed immersion. Suppose there is an exact sequence of fppf sheaves $$1\longrightarrow (\mathbf G_{m,F})^r\longrightarrow G\longrightarrow B\longrightarrow1$$ [def-pc-fppf-site], where $r\geq0$, $\mathbf G_{m,F}=\operatorname{Spec}F[t,t^{-1}]$ with multiplication, and $B/F$ is a proper smooth geometrically connected commutative group scheme. Geometrically connected means that every field extension gives a nonempty connected scheme [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]; proper is [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Exactness means that the left map identifies its source with the kernel and sections of $B$ lift fppf locally to $G$. For every integer $n\geq0$, the scheme $G^n=G\times_F\cdots\times_FG$, with $G^0=\operatorname{Spec}F$, is integral [def-pc-integral-scheme, def-pc-fibre-product]: it is nonempty, reduced and irreducible.

proof.text: For every field $L$, put $T_L=(\mathbf G_{m,L})^r$. Apply [lem-sfb-diagonalizable-group-geometric-criteria] to the free abelian group $\mathbf Z^r$: it has no nonzero torsion, so the stated characteristic-zero and positive-characteristic criteria both make $T_L$ smooth and geometrically connected, including $r=0$. It is affine by the group-algebra presentation in that statement. Over an affine $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq B$, the base change $T_B=T_F\times_F B$ has coordinate presentation $A[x_1,y_1,\ldots,x_r,y_r]/(x_i y_i-1)_{i=1}^r$; thus it is locally of finite presentation by [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence](1),(3) it is affine, quasi-compact and quasi-separated, hence of finite presentation by that same definition. Its smoothness follows by [lem-pc-proper-base-change](2), whose smooth clause requires no properness.

source.place: Examples 12.1--12.2, Proposition 12.3 and Remark 12.5, printed pp.231--232; explicit relative finite presentation; Stacks morphisms.tex Tags 01SD, 01S7 and 01VB

proof.text: Write $i:T_F\to G$ and $q:G\to B$ for the given homomorphisms. Regard the sheaf $h_G$ as a sheaf on $B$-schemes, with $T_B$ acting by $t\cdot g=i(t)g$. For any $B$-scheme $U$ and $g_1,g_2\in G(U)$ over the same section of $B$, $g_1g_2^{-1}$ lies in the kernel; exactness gives a unique $t\in T_F(U)$ with $i(t)=g_1g_2^{-1}$. This construction commutes with restriction. Local lifts of $\mathrm{id}_B$ exist on an fppf cover by the assumed epimorphism of sheaves. On a member with lift $s$, the maps $t\mapsto i(t)s$ and $g\mapsto i^{-1}(gs^{-1})$ give inverse equivariant sheaf isomorphisms with $h_{T_B}$. Consequently [lem-sfb-smooth-affine-group-torsor-representability], applied using Step 1, represents this sheaf by an affine smooth surjective universally open scheme over $B$. It is already represented by $G\to B$; [lem-galois-yoneda-fully-faithful] identifies the two representatives and their actions. Hence $q$ has those properties, and $(t,g)\mapsto(i(t)g,g)$ is an isomorphism $T_F\times_F G\simeq G\times_B G$.

source.place: Tags 0499 (lemma-characterize-trivial-pseudo-torsors), 049B (lemma-torsor), 049C (remark-fun-with-torsors), affine torsors; the kernel and inverse formulas are written out

proof.text: Fix $b\in B$, set $E=\kappa(b)$ and $X=G\times_B\operatorname{Spec}E$. The surjectivity of $q$ and [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change] make $X$ nonempty. Apply [lem-sfb-scheme-large-algclosed-jacobson] to $X/E$ to obtain an algebraically closed extension $\Omega/E$ for which closed points of $X_\Omega$ are dense and all have residue field $\Omega$. The same base-change-surjectivity lemma makes $X_\Omega$ nonempty. Its dense set of closed points is therefore nonempty; choose one. Its residue-field isomorphism gives a section $s:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X_\Omega$. Pulling the torsor isomorphism of Step 2 back to this fibre and fixing its second coordinate to $s$ gives inverse scheme maps $T_\Omega\to X_\Omega$, $t\mapsto i(t)s$, and $x\mapsto i^{-1}(xs^{-1})$. Thus $X_\Omega$ is connected by Step 1. By [lem-weil-geometrically-connected-algebraic-closure], which permits any algebraically closed extension and not only an algebraic one, $X/E$ is geometrically connected. No section over $E$ itself has been assumed.

source.place: Tag 0479 (lemma-make-Jacobson), Tag 0387 (lemma-characterize-geometrically-connected) with Tag 054N (lemma-geometrically-connected-check-after-extension); groupoids.tex Tag 0499, explicit translation trivialization

proof.text: By [def-pc-scheme-fibre], applied to $q:G\to B$ and $b$, the first projection is a homeomorphism from the scheme fibre $X=G\times_B\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(b)$ of Step 3 onto the subspace $q^{-1}(b)$ of $G$. Hence every topological fibre of $q$ is nonempty and connected. The map $q$ is open and surjective by Step 2, so it gives the quotient topology: if $q^{-1}(C)$ is closed, then $B\setminus C=q(G\setminus q^{-1}(C))$ is open, while the converse follows from continuity. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-connected-fibres-quotient-preimage-connected] with the closed connected subset $B$ itself. The assumed geometric connectedness of $B$ gives its nonempty connectedness, so $G$ is connected. Now [lem-weil-geometrically-connected-algebraic-closure], with the identity extension $F/F$ (allowed because $F$ is algebraically closed), makes $G$ geometrically connected over $F$.

proof.text: Induct on $n$ to prove that $G^n\to\operatorname{Spec}F$ is smooth. For $n=0$ the map is the identity of $\operatorname{Spec}F$: its finite presentation uses no variables or relations and every required infinitesimal lift is the given structure map, by [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. If $G^n$ is smooth, the projection $G^{n+1}=G\times_FG^n\to G^n$ is the base change of the assumed smooth structure morphism of $G$, so is smooth by [lem-pc-proper-base-change](2). Its composite with $G^n\to\operatorname{Spec}F$ is smooth by [lem-trf-smooth-composition]. This is the required structure morphism of $G^{n+1}$.

source.place: Tags 01VA (lemma-composition-smooth), 01VB (lemma-base-change-smooth); identity case from the definition

proof.text: For every field extension $K/F$ we prove, by induction on $n$, that $(G^n)_K$ is nonempty and connected. The base is $\operatorname{Spec}K$, a one-point space. Step 4 implies that $G_K$ is geometrically connected over $K$: every further extension $L/K$ is a field extension of $F$, and $(G_K)_L=G_L$. If $(G^n)_K$ is connected, [lem-weil-pbc-geometrically-connected-product-components], with $X=G_K$ and $Y=(G^n)_K$, gives a bijection on connected components from $G_K\times_K(G^n)_K$ to $(G^n)_K$. There is therefore exactly one component in the product, making it nonempty and connected. Associativity of fibre products identifies this product with $(G^{n+1})_K$: both represent tuples of $n+1$ points of $G$ over the same $K$-scheme. This proves geometric connectedness of $G^n$ for every $n$, including $0$.

source.place: Tag 0385 (lemma-bijection-connected-components); finite-product induction and fibre-product universal property written out

proof.text: Fix $n\geq0$ and apply [lem-trf-smooth-connected-fibre-normal-integrality] to $v:G^n\to\operatorname{Spec}F$. Smoothness is Step 5. There is just one base point, with residue field $F$; its scheme fibre is $G^n$ by the fibre-product universal property and is geometrically connected by Step 6. Taking $K=F$ in the cited conclusion shows that $G^n$ is integral. By [def-pc-integral-scheme] this says precisely that it is nonempty, reduced and irreducible. For $n=0$ it also follows directly because the only nonempty affine open of $\operatorname{Spec}F$ has coordinate ring the field $F$.
